title: Source tax tariff: children
purpose: Ask the child questions in one block per child (no maximum, age judged on the first working day). Derive each child's result (counted, counted with H, or not counted) and the child digit of the tariff code.

stories.title: Ask about children only of employees who need a source tax tariff
stories.i_want: to be asked about my children only when Lonio needs them to work out my source tax tariff code
stories.so_that: I give no personal data about my children that no receiving party needs, while the tariff code can still be computed without HR's manual calculator step
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a core goal (G-01) and the child questions feed the tariff code Lonio must compute for every employee subject to source tax (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Child step shown only after 'has children: yes'
acceptance_criteria.given: The employee is subject to source tax and answered the source tax details in step 6 'Source tax details' (for Liechtenstein residents: only if they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers whether they (for married employees and registered partners: they or their spouse/partner) have biological or adopted children
acceptance_criteria.then: Step 7 'Children' is shown only if the answer is 'yes'; with 'no', no child question is asked and the child digit of the tariff code is 0. Employees who are not subject to source tax, and Liechtenstein residents whose answers mean 'in principle no source tax liability', are never asked about children. The child answers go to no party as such; they are used only to derive the source tax tariff code recorded for HR.

stories.title: One block per child: age status and household
stories.i_want: to describe each of my children in their own block, starting with whether the child is a minor or an adult in first education and whether the child lives in my household
stories.so_that: every child is judged on its own, as in the Zurich calculator, and children who cannot count end the block at once without further questions
stories.priority_reason: The per-child answers decide the child digit of the tariff code Lonio computes instead of HR (D-001); a wrong count gives a wrong tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: One block per child, no maximum
acceptance_criteria.given: The employee answered 'yes' to having biological or adopted children
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee fills in one block per child and can add another block or remove one; there is no maximum number of children. Assumption (D-044), to be verified by a domain expert: no maximum applies.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child's age status, judged on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the first question of the block
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee must choose one of 'Minor', 'Adult and in first education' or 'Neither'; the answer is required. The child's age is judged on the employee's first working day. Assumption (D-044), to be verified by a domain expert: the first working day is the reference date.

acceptance_criteria.title: 'Neither' ends the block; the child does not count
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers 'Neither' (neither a minor nor an adult in first education)
acceptance_criteria.then: No further question is asked for this child and the child does not count towards the tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Same household asked for minors and adults in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: The child is a minor or an adult in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the child block
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether the child lives in their household; the answer is required and decides which further questions follow for this child.

stories.title: Minor child living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask, for a minor child in the employee's household, about custody, a common household with the other parent, alternating custody and the larger financial contributor, and to derive the child's result as the calculator does
stories.so_that: the child is counted, counted with H (single parents) or not counted exactly as in the Zurich calculator
stories.priority_reason: Lonio replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001); a wrong per-child result gives a wrong tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: The child is a minor and lives in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the child block
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee must state parental custody ('Shared custody' or 'Sole custody'). Only with shared custody: whether they live in a common household with the other parent (yes/no). Only without a common household: whether there is alternating custody (yes/no). Who makes the larger financial contribution ('Me' or 'The other parent') is asked when there is alternating custody, or - for employees who are single, divorced, widowed or separated - when they live in a common household with the other parent. Every answer is required when asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Result for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: The employee is married or in a registered partnership and the child is a minor in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: The child is counted with sole custody, or with shared custody and a common household with the other parent, or with alternating custody where the employee is the larger contributor (this last row is inferred, not observed, and is checked before go-live, D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage). Otherwise it is not counted. Where an observed calculator run exists it wins over the derived logic (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Result for single, divorced, widowed and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: The employee is single, divorced, widowed or separated and the child is a minor in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: The child is counted with H with sole custody; with shared custody and a common household with the other parent when the employee is the larger contributor; with shared custody, no common household and no alternating custody; or with alternating custody where the employee is the larger contributor. When the other parent is the larger contributor the child is not counted (with alternating custody this row is inferred and checked before go-live, D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage). Observed calculator runs win over the derived logic (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert).

stories.title: Minor child not living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask, for a minor child outside the employee's household, about shared custody (married) or parental care (not married), alternating custody and the larger financial contributor, and to derive the child's result as the calculator does
stories.so_that: a child living elsewhere counts only where the calculator counts it
stories.priority_reason: Lonio replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001); a wrong per-child result gives a wrong tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for a minor child outside the household
acceptance_criteria.given: The child is a minor and does not live in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the child block
acceptance_criteria.then: Employees who are married or in a registered partnership must answer whether custody is shared (yes/no); employees who are single, divorced, widowed or separated must answer whether they have parental care (yes/no). Only with 'yes': whether there is alternating custody (yes/no); only with alternating custody: who makes the larger financial contribution ('Me' or 'The other parent'). Custody of a child in the household is not asked. Every answer is required when asked. Registered partnership counts as married and Separated as single (assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Result for a minor child outside the household
acceptance_criteria.given: The child is a minor outside the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.then: The child counts only with shared custody (married) or parental care (not married), alternating custody and the employee as the larger contributor: married employees get 'counted', the others 'counted with H'. In every other case it is not counted. The rows 'alternating custody with the other parent contributing more' and 'no alternating custody' are inferred and checked before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage); observed calculator runs win over the derived logic (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert).

stories.title: Adult child in first education
stories.i_want: Lonio to ask, for an adult child in first education, about a common household with the other parent, the larger financial contributor and whether the employee provides more than 50% of the maintenance, and to derive the child's result as the calculator does
stories.so_that: adult children in first education count exactly where the calculator counts them
stories.priority_reason: Lonio replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001); a wrong per-child result gives a wrong tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for an adult child in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: The child is an adult in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues the child block
acceptance_criteria.then: If the child lives in the household, the employee must answer whether they live in a common household with the other parent (yes/no). Employees who are single, divorced, widowed or separated and live with the other parent are asked who makes the larger financial contribution ('Me' or 'The other parent'). Whether the employee mainly (more than 50%) provides for the child's maintenance (yes/no) is asked when the child lives outside the household or there is no common household with the other parent. Custody and alternating custody are not asked. Every answer is required when asked. Registered partnership counts as married and Separated as single (assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.given: The employee is married or in a registered partnership and the child is an adult in first education
acceptance_criteria.then: The child is counted with a common household with the other parent, or when the employee provides more than 50% of the maintenance; otherwise not counted. Rows not observed in the calculator are inferred and checked before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage); observed runs win over the derived logic (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Result for single, divorced, widowed and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: The employee is single, divorced, widowed or separated and the child is an adult in first education
acceptance_criteria.then: A child in the household is counted with H when the employee is the larger contributor (common household with the other parent) or provides more than 50% of the maintenance (no common household); otherwise not counted. Rows not observed in the calculator are inferred and checked before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage); observed runs win over the derived logic (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert).

stories.title: Child digit of the tariff code and go-live check of the child paths
stories.i_want: Lonio to set the child digit of the source tax tariff code to the number of children who count, and to have the child paths not yet observed in the calculator checked before go-live
stories.so_that: the recorded tariff code (e.g. 'C3Y') matches the calculator without HR clicking through it
stories.priority_reason: The child digit is part of every tariff code Lonio computes in place of HR (D-001); unverified paths must be checked before release (D-009).

acceptance_criteria.title: Each counted child adds one to the child digit
acceptance_criteria.given: The employee is subject to source tax and has completed the child blocks
acceptance_criteria.then: Each child whose result is 'counted' or 'counted with H' adds one to the child digit; a child that is not counted adds nothing. With three counted children the digit is 3 (e.g. 'C3Y'). Without children the digit is 0. There is no maximum number of children (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert). The digit is always derived again from the latest answers.

Child counted with H adds one (single, sole custody)
Child neither minor nor in first education adds nothing
Child not counted adds nothing (married, no shared custody)

acceptance_criteria.title: Go-live check of the child paths
acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio derives per-child results and the child digit
acceptance_criteria.when: the feature is prepared for go-live
acceptance_criteria.then: A domain expert compares Lonio's results with the Zurich calculator for the per-child rows marked inferred and for more than 3 children (see OQ-calculator-coverage, a non-blocking go-live condition). Until then, observed calculator runs win over the derived logic (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert).
